title: Linen & Laundry Safety
blurb: Staying safe with linen and in the laundry: hidden sharps, soiled linen, heavy loads and hot machines.
siteNotes: The venue's sharps procedure: who to tell and how a sharp is made safe.
Where gloves are kept and which laundry chemicals are used, with their COSHH information.
Where trolleys are kept and any slopes or lifts to take care in.
legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer says to follow "the sharps procedure". Confirm the venue has a written procedure (including what to do after a needlestick or cut) and add it to the site notes.
Manual handling (Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992) and COSHH (COSHH Regulations 2002) are mentioned in the trainer; no figures are stated.

cards.title: Linen & Laundry Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- avoid injury from sharps hidden in linen
- handle soiled linen and heavy loads safely
- spot the hazards in the laundry area

cards.title: Linen looks harmless
cards.body: Handling linen looks harmless, but it hides several real risks. The biggest surprise is sharp objects hidden in bed linen and towels: guests occasionally leave needles, razors, broken glass or other sharps wrapped up in the sheets.

cards.title: Never plunge your hands in
cards.body:
Never plunge your hands into a bundle of linen or press it down into a bag or trolley. Strip beds carefully and watch what you are doing.

If you find a sharp, do not grab it. Report it and follow the sharps procedure.

right.title: Do not
items: Press linen down into a bag
Put a sharp in your pocket

cards.title: Treat it as contaminated
cards.body: Treat soiled linen especially cautiously. Wear gloves, and handle it as though it could be contaminated, because it can carry bacteria or bodily fluids.

items.title: Assume contaminated
items.text: It can carry bacteria or fluids

cards.title: Wet laundry is heavy
cards.body:
Wet laundry is heavy, so use trolleys and do not overload them. Lift bags using good technique rather than dragging or hauling.

Keep trolleys under control on slopes and in lifts.

items.title: Good technique
items.text: Lift, do not drag or haul

cards.title: Hot machines and chemicals
cards.body:
The laundry area has hot machines, irons and chemicals. Beware hot surfaces and steam, follow the machine instructions, and use laundry chemicals safely (COSHH).

Keep the area tidy to avoid slips and trips.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never plunge your hands into a bundle of linen or press it down.
- Wear gloves and treat soiled linen as though it could be contaminated.
- If you find a sharp, report it and follow the sharps procedure.
- Use trolleys, do not overload them, and lift with good technique.
- Mind hot surfaces, steam and chemicals (COSHH), and keep the area tidy.

cards.q: Sharp objects like needles or glass can be hidden in bed linen.
cards.why: Guests occasionally leave needles, razors, broken glass or other sharps wrapped up in the sheets.

cards.q: When handling a bundle of linen you should…
options: Plunge your hands in to check it over
Never plunge your hands in; handle it carefully
Press it down hard to fit more in
Shake it out quickly over the bed
cards.why: Never plunge your hands into a bundle of linen or press it down into a bag or trolley.

cards.q: What should you wear when handling soiled linen?
options: Just an apron
Nothing if you wash your hands later
A hairnet and overshoes
Gloves
cards.why: Wear gloves, and handle soiled linen as though it could be contaminated.

cards.q: Soiled linen should be treated as though it could be contaminated.
cards.why: It can carry bacteria or bodily fluids, so treat it as though it could be contaminated.

cards.q: If you find a sharp in the linen you should…
options: Report it and follow the sharps procedure
Grab it quickly and bin it
Put it in your pocket until later
Leave it in the linen for the laundry
cards.why: Do not grab it. Report it and follow the sharps procedure.

cards.q: Wet laundry is heavy, so you should use trolleys and good lifting technique.
cards.why: Wet laundry is heavy. Use trolleys, do not overload them, and lift with good technique.

cards.q: Which of these is a hazard in the laundry area itself?
options: Low lighting at night
Quiet working hours
Hot machines, irons and steam
A noisy corridor
cards.why: The laundry area has hot machines, irons, steam and chemicals, and slip and trip risks.

cards.q: It is fine to overload a laundry trolley to save trips.
cards.why: Do not overload trolleys. Use them properly and keep them under control.

options: In any way that is quickest
Safely, following COSHH
Mixed together for a stronger clean
By eye, without reading the label
cards.why: Use laundry chemicals safely, following COSHH.

cards.q: Keeping the laundry area tidy helps avoid slips and trips.
cards.why: Keep the area tidy to avoid slips and trips.
